paragraphs: Moths have long been described as the helpless prey of bats, but several species have evolved ears tuned to the ultrasonic calls that bats use to locate food. A moth that hears an approaching bat may fold its wings and dive, and a few species go further by answering with clicks of their own. Researchers disagree about the purpose of the clicks. Some hold that the clicks startle the bat and give the moth time to escape. Others suggest that the clicks scramble the returning echo, so that the bat misjudges where the moth is. The second proposal has been tested less, and I suspect it will prove the more important, since startle responses fade quickly when a predator meets the same signal again and again.
